standard_prerequisites.name: Computable enumerability via a computable relation
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the enumerability half: K_1 = {e : exists s T(e,0,s)} is presented by a computable relation T(e,0,s).

standard_prerequisites.name: Universal partial computable function and the s-m-n theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: There is a universal partial computable function Un(e,x) = phi_e(x), and the s-m-n theorem supplies a primitive recursive index s(e,x,y) with phi_{s(e,x,y)}(z) = phi_e[3](x,y,z).
standard_prerequisites.use: Both are the constructive core: the index e with phi_e[3](x,y,z) = phi_x(y) is picked via universality, and s-m-n fixes the input x, y into the index so that halting on 0 mirrors phi_x(y).

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1528-1535): K_1 = {e : phi_e(0) converges} is computably enumerable but not computable.
Enumerability (proof lines 1537-1540): K_1 = {e : exists s T(e,0,s)} is c.e. by the exists-characterisation (stub thm:exists-char).

Reduction K_0 <=_m K_1 (lines 1542-1595): universality gives e with phi_e[3](x,y,z) = phi_x(y); s-m-n gives primitive recursive s(e,x,y) with phi_{s(e,x,y)}(z) = phi_x(y); hence phi_{s(e,x,y)}(0) converges iff phi_x(y) converges, so g(w) = s(e,(w)_0,(w)_1) is a many-one reduction of K_0 to K_1.
proof_roadmap: Present K_1 as a projection of the halting relation T(e,0,s) and cite the exists-characterisation.
Build the index e for the 3-ary function (x,y,z) |-> phi_x(y) by universality.
Apply s-m-n to s(e,x,y), evaluate at z = 0, and read off g(w) = s(e,(w)_0,(w)_1) as the reduction.
difficulty_reason: Halting set K_1 (statement 1528-1535, proof 1537-1595): enumerability via the exists-characterisation plus a full s-m-n reduction construction with an oracle-style motivational explain; every constructive step is in-span. H3.
